questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a place with a vibrant city with lots to do. I think Vienna displayed this exactly with its great reputation as well as being one of the oldest universitys in Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My expectations were met completely - loved Vienna!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The mobility team from the University of Vienna were very accomodating with providing the needed information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a mandatory intro meeting where all information about the stay was provided - very informative.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They were easy to reach and very quick to respond, so this was nice.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used AirBnB which was quite easy, but also quite expensive. Would probably check Facebook for cheaper accomodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most areas are quite nice to live in. I would focus on the 1st-9th district and perhaps the 15th and 16th.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were plenty of options available.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy. They made it very clear what information was needed and made the registration process smooth.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Met up at the university before the first lectures and got info about everything about registration process for courses and what needed to be done during and after the exchange.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Contact through email or at their office at the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of them - you get 1000 points you can split up into your preferences for courses. But I also chose some courses based on the fact that a lot people wanted to get them, so I had a higher chance of getting them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Listen to the intro - they tell what you need to be aware off.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Same level as back home. So you should expect that you need to a bit of schoolwork to pass the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures. No classes with a TA where you could ask questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Topics in Valuation
Environmental Economics
Management - Organization and Personnel
Asset Pricing 1
Financial Crisis
Contract, coordination, and incentives
Economic Analysis of Law

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Financial Crisis. Was interesting and the professor was really nice and interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, it was quite easy to manage the costs since they didnt differ significantly from Copenhagen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Shopping and eating out is a bit less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were quite a lot of opportunities if wanted to join clubs - they had so many choices.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had so many different types of clubs and social activities through Erasmus. So you could do something every day basically if you wanted to.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Erasmus-events. You meet so many people from all over.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other cities. You have Budapest, Bratislava, and Ljubljana close - I went there and it was so nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Not that different from Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the Erasmus-events. People are there to socialize as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing. I feel most European cultures are quite similar.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, beer, and the bars and going out. Super cool.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy food, explore city, try new things.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I rented a bike for the first months, that was quite nice. And go there early in the summer if go in the fall - the city was amazing in late summer.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New culture and getting to know a completely new city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from home, but you get used to it quite quickly with new friends etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy the stay!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
